decision_summary.text: Whether to investigate Northline's reporting need now while protecting reliability and smaller-customer commitments.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I keep moving between “this is how good products learn” and “we are letting the loudest customer set the roadmap.”

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: My provisional plan is to offer Northline three focused sessions over the next two weeks, document the workflow, and explicitly make no build commitment.

positions.text: Run bounded discovery with Northline without beginning the build, while making reliability and core-workflow commitments visible before deciding.

contributions.speaker: assistant
contributions.quote: That supports a narrower move—capture the workflow and test the reusable concept now without beginning full implementation.

contributions.speaker: user
contributions.quote: My provisional plan is to offer Northline three focused sessions over the next two weeks, document the workflow, and explicitly make no build commitment.

contributions.speaker: assistant
contributions.quote: You can decide in advance what kind of disposable prototype is allowed and ask Northline to reflect back what they believe the sessions mean.

threads.text: Whether formal discovery boundaries will damage the informal trust Northline earned through early support.

introduced.speaker: user
introduced.quote: If I suddenly arrive with a formal evaluation boundary, it could feel like we have become bureaucratic just when they need us.

responses.speaker: assistant
responses.quote: You do not need to present a governance ceremony.

responses.speaker: assistant
responses.quote: The two risks you named remain real: restricting prototypes may make discovery artificial, while careful language may still feel like distance to Northline.

latest_ref.speaker: assistant
latest_ref.quote: Neither step guarantees trust or a good product decision, but both make misunderstanding easier to notice before momentum chooses for you.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I run product for a nine-person software company.

constraints.text: Reliability work has already been postponed twice.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: we have reliability work we have postponed twice

constraints.text: Smaller customers were promised a simpler core workflow in the next release.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: we told smaller customers that the next release would simplify the core workflow

constraints.text: Lina believes roughly seventy percent of the reporting work could be reusable.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Lina, our strongest engineer, thinks about seventy percent of the underlying work could become a general reporting layer.

constraints.text: Sales has already signaled serious consideration of a summer path without calling it a promise.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: our sales lead has already told them we are “looking seriously at a summer path.” He says that is not a promise.

constraints.text: Lina is one of two people carrying on-call and was hit hard by the last incident.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Lina is excited, but she is also one of two people carrying on-call, and the last incident hit her hard.

constraints.text: Delivery can wait one quarter, but the operations lead who knows the problem may leave the role.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: They can live with their manual CSV process for another quarter, although their operations lead may move to a different role by then.

constraints.text: Smaller customers currently want fewer confusing states and faster support, not reporting.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Our smaller customers are not asking for reporting. They are asking for fewer confusing states and faster support.
